title: Neutralinojs desktop app setup with a narrow allow list
when: The user wants a small cross platform desktop app from HTML, CSS and JavaScript with Neutralinojs and needs a config that exposes only the native calls it uses.
prompt:
Goal: A Neutralinojs project whose neutralino.config.json opens one window, serves resources/ and allows only the native functions the code calls.
Steps:
1. Run neu create notes-desk, or create neutralino.config.json, resources/index.html, resources/js/main.js and resources/js/neutralino.js.
2. Root keys: "applicationId": "com.acme.notesdesk", "version": "1.0.0", "defaultMode": "window", "documentRoot": "/resources/", "url": "/", "enableNativeAPI": true, "tokenSecurity": "one-time".
3. "nativeAllowList": list exact functions such as "app.exit", "os.showOpenDialog", "filesystem.readFile", "filesystem.writeFile"; never "os.*" or "*".
4. "modes": { "window": { "title": "Notes", "width": 960, "height": 640, "minWidth": 480, "minHeight": 360 } }.
5. "cli": { "binaryName": "notes-desk", "resourcesPath": "/resources/", "clientLibrary": "/resources/js/neutralino.js" }.
6. main.js: Neutralino.init(); Neutralino.events.on("windowClose", () => Neutralino.app.exit()).
7. Develop with neu run; neu build --release writes dist/notes-desk/ with binaries and resources.neu.
Quality bar:
- Every native call in the code appears in the allow list, and nothing more.
Pitfalls:
- Allowing os.execCommand, which turns any injected script into shell access.
- Forgetting the windowClose handler, so the process keeps running.
Verify:
- [ ] neutralino.config.json parses with applicationId and modes.window.
- [ ] nativeAllowList has no wildcard on os.
- [ ] neutralino.js is loaded before main.js.
Output: neutralino.config.json, resources/index.html and resources/js/main.js.

examples.input: quero um app desktop leve com HTML e JS
examples.output: Neutralinojs project with one-time token, window 960x640 min 480x360, five exact allow list entries
